---
title: Choosing templates
description: Which templates to combine for a project, and monolith or monorepo for the front end.
---

import Diagram from '../../../components/Diagram.astro';

A project is usually two to four generated repositories: an API, a front end,
and a worker per kind of background work, or an API and its Node worker
generated together as one monorepo.

| You need | Generate |
|---|---|
| An HTTP API, auth, a database | `nest-api` |
| A web front end | `react-app` (or `react-monorepo`, below) |
| A site its owner edits, or a small shop, with no API of its own | `next-site`, on its own ([below](#a-site-or-an-app)) |
| Slow or heavy jobs outside the API process | `node-worker` |
| The API and a Node worker sharing one database | `nest-monorepo` (one repository, one Prisma package; [why](nest-monorepo/#a-monorepo-or-two-repositories)) |
| Jobs that need Python libraries | `py-worker` |
| Durable, multi-step workflows | `--with temporal` on the API and a worker ([why](../guides/background-work/)) |

<Diagram name="full-stack" title="A full stacks project and the services it runs on" height={640} />

## Monolith or monorepo

`react-app` and `react-monorepo` are the same code: react-app is generated from
the monorepo's packages. The choice is about deployment, not code.

| | react-app | react-monorepo |
|---|---|---|
| Deployments | one image | one image per app |
| Auth screens | routes (`/login`) | their own app and origin |
| Session | a plain cookie on one origin | one cookie shared across subdomains |
| Releases | together | each app independently |
| Moving parts | fewer | cookie domain, trusted origins, CORS for every app |

Start with **react-app**. Move to the monorepo when surfaces genuinely need to
ship on different schedules, scale separately, or be locked down on their own
(an admin console reachable only from a VPN, a marketing site edited daily).

## A site or an app

[`next-site`](next-site/) stands alone: Next.js with Payload CMS built in, its
own Postgres, its own auth, no API to generate or deploy. It is for the site a
business edits itself: company pages, a portfolio, a small shop
(`--with shop`) paid outside the site. Choose the API and front-end templates
above instead when the product needs an API of its own: mobile or third-party
clients, background jobs, roles and workflows beyond content and orders.

| | next-site | react-app + nest-api |
|---|---|---|
| Repositories and deployments | one | two or more |
| Content edited by | the owner, in Payload's admin | developers, or an admin you build |
| Data model | Payload collections | Prisma models behind an API |
| Payments | `manual` built in, others as adapters | yours to build |

## How they connect

| Link | Setting that must match |
|---|---|
| Front end → API | the front end's `VITE_APP_API_URL`; the API's `FRONTEND_HOST` (and `MISC_CORS_ORIGINS`) |
| API ↔ workers (jobs) | the same `REDIS_*`, and the same queue names on both sides |
| API ↔ workers (data) | the same database; the worker's models match the API's schema (automatic in `nest-monorepo`) |
| API → Temporal → workers | the same `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS` and `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`; the worker polls the task queue the API starts on |
| Everything → OpenObserve | one org per project, a distinct `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` per service |

Mismatches are mostly silent: a worker on the wrong Redis connects happily and
never receives a job. [A full-stack project](../guides/full-stack/) walks
through each link.
